rulings.model: Only the 50% and 80% categories are provided. The instructions also say 'you can fully deduct meals and incidentals furnished or reimbursed to an employee if you properly treat the expense as wages', and likewise for amounts reported on Form 1099-NEC. These 100% meals have no place, and no refusal names them.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope gap recorded; restatement accepted for the meals it asks. Meals fully deductible (treated as wages, or reported on Form 1099-NEC; i1040sc p. 10) have no input; a filer who entered them at 50% would understate the deduction. Left for the owner as TASKS.md T-042 (a 100% input or a refusal).

rulings.restated: Input — Did you "materially participate" in the operation of this business during 2025 (for example, you worked in it more than 500 hours, or your work was substantially all the work done in it, or more than 100 hours and at least as much as anyone else; see the seven tests in the instructions for line G), and is the business something other than a rental activity?
rulings.model: The restatement leaves out the oil and gas exception. The IRS text says to check Yes if 'you meet any of the material participation tests ... or the exception for oil and gas applies', and a working interest 'is not a passive activity'. Such a filer would answer No and be refused as passive, which the refusal does not name.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: fixed (BUG-0064). The question now includes the exception for oil and gas (i1040sc p. 4, line G; p. 5, Exception for oil and gas), so a working interest is answered Yes and not refused as passive.
